title: Children, Families, and Communities
gist: A RAND topic hub page (Children, Families, and Communities) listing recent research teasers rather than a single article; the most decision-relevant item is RAND American Life Panel data showing parental AI use jumped from 54% in 2025 to 72% in 2026, reaching 84% in households earning $150,000+. Other teasers flag Santa Monica's steeper retail/tourism declines versus LA peers and a RAND Europe paper on the UK adapting Sweden's Total Defence model.

themes.theme: Income-skewed AI adoption among US families

insights.claim: RAND American Life Panel survey data show the share of US parents using artificial intelligence for work or personal reasons rose from 54% in 2025 to 72% in 2026.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: An 18-point one-year jump in household AI usage signals rapid mainstream consumer adoption, supportive of consumer-facing AI demand.
insights.quote: The share of parents using artificial intelligence for work or personal reasons rose from 54% in 2025 to 72% in 2026.
insights.locator: Higher-Income Parents More Likely to Use AI

insights.claim: Among US families earning $150,000 or more, parental AI usage reached 84% in 2026, and those higher-income parents were more likely than lower-income parents to encourage their teens to use AI for schoolwork.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: AI adoption is stratifying by income, implying an emerging education/skills gap and a premium-household skew for AI consumer products and edtech.
insights.quote: But that number jumped to 84% in families earning $150,000 or more.
insights.locator: Higher-Income Parents More Likely to Use AI

insights.claim: A RAND cross-sectional survey of US parents examined how comfortable they are with AI-led behavioral therapy for their children and which factors predict greater comfort, signaling that AI in child mental-health care is now an active area of policy research.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Parental acceptance is a gating factor for AI digital-therapeutics adoption in pediatric behavioral health; watch the findings.
insights.locator: Parent Comfort With Artificial Intelligence-Led Behavioral Therapy

themes.theme: Local economic divergence and pandemic-aid evaluation

insights.claim: RAND researchers found Santa Monica experienced steeper declines in retail sales and tourism than peer cities near Los Angeles, though recent policy reforms may improve the city's economic trajectory.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Relevant for Southern California retail real estate and hospitality exposure; underperformance versus peers may be reversible if reforms take hold.
insights.quote: They found steeper declines in retail sales and tourism, but recent policy reforms may improve the city’s economic trajectory.
insights.locator: Santa Monica’s Recent Economic and Social Trends

insights.claim: RAND is evaluating the collective impact of expanded COVID-era US financial assistance for low-income households and households with children on food security and financial wellbeing, across expansions of three policies.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Evidence on pandemic transfer effectiveness will inform debates over reviving expanded child or household benefits, which affect consumer spending at the low end.
insights.locator: Pandemic Financial Assistance and Household Wellbeing

insights.claim: A RAND Europe paper argues the UK can pragmatically adapt lessons from Sweden's decade-long rebuilding of Total Defence since 2015 to strengthen national resilience and warfighting readiness amid rising European security concerns.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
insights.so_what: Whole-of-society defence models imply sustained European spending on civil resilience, defence readiness and critical infrastructure.
insights.quote: how the UK can pragmatically adapt lessons from Sweden's decade-long rebuilding of Total Defence since 2015
insights.locator: Strengthening UK national resilience and warfighting readiness

insights.claim: RAND economist Lisa Abraham's research compares how veterans' and non-veterans' earnings evolve over time in the civilian workforce, a subject RAND highlighted around Veterans Day 2026.
insights.speaker: RAND Corporation
entities: RAND Epstein Family Veterans Policy Research Institute
insights.so_what: Signals continued policy focus on veteran workforce transition; minor relevance for labor-market supply analysis.
insights.locator: How Do Veterans Fare in the Civilian Workforce?
